# Jet engine (gas turbine) (`jet_engine`)

<!-- generated by scripts/build_techtree.py from techtree/core/navigation.yaml — do not edit -->

- Category: Navigation, transport & exploration (`navigation`)
- Deps: helped by steam_turbine, glider_aeroplane, laws_of_motion
- Core idea: A rotary compressor squeezes air, fuel burns continuously in it, the hot gas drives a turbine that turns the compressor, and the remaining gas leaves at high speed through a nozzle, pushing the aircraft forward by reaction. It is light for its power and works best at high speed and altitude; the hard part is turbine blades that survive red heat under huge centrifugal loads (nickel alloys).
- Pitfalls:
  - Thinking the jet 'pushes against the air behind it'; thrust is the reaction to accelerating the gas
  - Ignoring the turbine temperature limit; ordinary steels creep and fail within minutes
  - Confusing it with the rocket, which carries its own oxidiser and works in vacuum
- History: europe: 1930 – Frank Whittle's patent; 1937 his engine runs; 27 Aug 1939 Heinkel He 178 (von Ohain) first jet flight; 1944 Me 262 and Gloster Meteor in service
- Read:
  - Frank Whittle, Jet: The Story of a Pioneer (1953)
  - Edward W. Constant II, The Origins of the Turbojet Revolution (1980)
